sources.note: 17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a selectboard
Town of Woodstock, Town Selectboard page (live): Norm Frates Jr. (Chair, to 2029), MaryAnn Sweeney (Vice Chair, to 2028), Susan Chiefsky (to 2027), Ben Ford (to 2027), and Clay Reed (to 2027)

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): the report's post-March-2025 roster (Bourgeois, Susan Ford, Cole, Cliff Johnson, Powell) has entirely turned over; the exit mechanisms are unpublished. The town's live page governs; the factory's four-name set and the Secretary of State directory's lone 'Susan Ford' are stale (disclosed)
17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a town clerk
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists F. Charles Degener III as Woodstock's Town Clerk

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): Town Clerk F. Charles Degener (printed term to 2026); the 2026 warning carried a three-year clerk term and the live page still names him, so he is carried on incumbent-continuity (disclosed)
17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a town treasurer

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): Town Treasurer F. 17 V.S.A. section 2646 establishes the office (towns elect a moderator for a one-year term); no official source publishes the current holder, so the post is created without a membership

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): Moderator Matthew Maxham (printed term to 2026); the 2026 warning carried the moderator election but the outcome is unpublished, so no holder is minted; Maxham is carried as a straggler on issue #163

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): Cemetery Commissioners Gregory Camp (to 2027) and two seats printed VACANT (expiring 2026 and 2028); the 2026 warning carried three-year and two-year cemetery seats with the outcomes unpublished, so only Camp is minted

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists ten Woodstock justices of the peace: Fred Barr, Susan Chiefsky, Rick Fiske, David Green, Matt Maxham, Jan Noskey, Michael Ricci, Mary Riley, Bill Boardman, and Jill Davies (Davies's entry continues across the listing's pp. 42-43 page break)

Town of Woodstock, 2026 Annual Town Report, Elected Officials table and 2026 warning (Article 9): the report's justices table names twelve, adding Jane Soule, Catie Baumgartner, and BJ Dunn and omitting certified winners Jan Noskey and Michael Ricci; the certified slate governs and the table is disclosed on issue #163

jp_election.name: Town of Woodstock Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): certifies the November 5, 2024 election of ten justices of the peace for Woodstock: Fred Barr, Susan Chiefsky, Rick Fiske, David Green, Matt Maxham, Jan Noskey, Michael Ricci, Mary Riley, Bill Boardman, and Jill Davies. NOTE: the town's auditors were eliminated by the March 1, 2025 vote (Article 14), so no auditor post is created
